changes: Seated the fixed holder on the stage and under the existing slide; adjusted its screws and added the retaining-pivot support stem without moving specimen or optical datums.
Added convex-prism compounds following the actual rounded concave holder and retaining-arm footprints, plus pivot/lever/screw contacts.
Removed four obsolete generic holder-ring colliders that otherwise created an invisible ledge 0.7 mm above the repaired holder.
Matched the projecting thumb lever bevel and objective distal tapers with convex contact meshes, replacing an invisible early focus stop with measured surface contact.
baseline_findings: The fixed holder penetrated the glass slide by 0.6 mm and floated above its deck mounting.
Eleven sampled detailed holder/objective intersection poses lacked a native contact.
limitations: Exterior dimensions, loads, material properties and holder/stand relief dimensions remain reconstruction estimates; no manufacturer CAD or metrology is claimed.
Collision checks cover the named assemblies and finite sampled poses, not every possible configuration or every inserted screw/bearing seam.
Native contact is numerically soft; contact regressions measure and limit penetration rather than interpreting it as calibrated material indentation.
The optical-axis check is geometric. Internal optical prescriptions and lower condenser transmission are not ray-traced.
Existing cable models and renderer behavior are preserved; these repairs do not add robot-driven cable dynamics.
